# Practical Exercise: Fractional factorial experiment 


## Aims of this practical exercise


In this exercise you will:

- use tools for $2^k$ experiments in a fractionated experiment setting.

## Before you undertake this exercise...


Get the necessary add-on packages:


## Banking Example

Source: Ch 9 "Case Studies", Pages 129-209, of Antony, J. (2023)  Design of Experiments for Engineers and Scientists (Third Edition), Elsevier. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B978044315173600024X

The bank in this exercise was experiencing a 60% reprocessing rate on applications due to incomplete information provided by customers. 


Factors	| Labels	| Low level	| High level
--- | --- | --- | --- 
Application type	| A	| Loan	| Lease
Region	| B	| Midwest	| Northeast
Description	| C	| Current	| Enhanced (additional explanation provided)
Example	| D	| Current	| Enhanced (additional examples provided)
Negative example	| E	| None	| Yes


``` {r}
Banking = read.csv("Banking.csv") |> mutate(across(A:E, as.factor)) |>
glimpse()
```


## Required

Q: How fractionated is this experiment?
There are five factors in 16 runs, so it is a half fraction.

```{r}
MyDesign = FrF2(nruns = 16, nfactors = 5, randomize = FALSE)
MyDesign
```

```{r}
Banking
```



Q: Which effects are aliased? Hint: look at the (correct) ANOVA table to see which effects you **can** estimate.
```{r}
Banking.full = lm(Average.percentage.complete~A*B*C*D*E, data=Banking)
aliases(Banking.full)
Banking.full |> anova()
```


Q: Which effects are significant?

Appears that factors C and D are significant. as they deviate from the reference striagh line (Daniel plot) and thex exceed the ME and SME in Lenth plot. 
```{r}
DanielPlot((Banking.full), half = TRUE)
```

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=6}
# BsMD::LenthPlot(Banking.full)

# Extract coefficients (excluding intercept) and remove NAs
effects <- coef(Banking.full)[-1]
effects_clean <- effects[!is.na(effects)]

# Generate Lenth plot
BsMD::LenthPlot(effects_clean, yaxt = "n", ylab = "effects")
axis(side = 2, las = 2) 
```

```{r}
all(is.finite(coef(Banking.full)[-1]))
class(coef(Banking.full)[-1])


any(is.na(Banking.full$coefficients))
is.numeric(coef(Banking.full)[-1])
```



```{r}
MEPlot(Banking.full)

```


```{r}
IAPlot(Banking.full, select = 1:5)
```


Q: What are the recommendations resulting from this experiment?
You need more data points. 

```{r}
Banking.2= lm(Average.percentage.complete~C+D, data=Banking)
aliases(Banking.2)
Banking.2 |> anova()
```

```{r}
plot(Banking.2)
```
```{r}
emm <- emmeans::emmeans(Banking.2, ~ C*D)
pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey")
plot(emm)
```
the two factors that matter are Description and example. When the data have enhanced and enhanced they vary significantly. Enhanced has higher average completion rate.
